2609.29940.title: Mind What Matters for Reasoning: Aligning Cross-Modal Attention via Selective Probability Mass Concentration
2609.29940.paper_summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) achieve strong performance on visual reasoning tasks, yet remain prone to hallucinations and over-reliance on language priors, often generating answers without adequately using task-relevant visual evidence. Existing approaches primarily improve reasoning through reasoning-oriented supervision or inference-time strategies. In this work, we study a complementary question: can multimodal reasoning be improved by strengthening implicit visual grounding without directly supervising the reasoning process? Motivated by the functional specialization of attention heads, we investigate whether reasoning can be improved by guiding only the heads most responsive to visual evidence grounding. We propose Selective Probability Mass Concentration (sPMC), a training framework that identifies grounding-responsive heads and selectively regularizes their text-to-image attention. sPMC treats normalized attention over visual tokens as a spatial probability distribution and encourages the probability mass to be assigned to semantically relevant regions using segmentation-derived spatial priors. Adaptive Head Selection restricts this guidance to visually responsive heads while leaving the remaining heads unconstrained to preserve their complementary functions. Across 6 multimodal benchmark suites, sPMC achieves an average zero-shot improvement of 3% and gains of up to 11.3% across multiple MLLMs while regularizing only 3%-15% of their attention heads. These results demonstrate that targeted guidance of sparse and implicit visual evidence pathways can directly improve multimodal reasoning.
2609.29940.paper_summary_zh: 多模態大型語言模型（MLLMs）在視覺推理任務上表現優異，但仍然容易出現幻覺和過度依賴語言先驗，經常在沒有充分利用與任務相關的視覺證據的情況下生成答案。現有的方法主要通過以推理為導向的監督或推理時間策略來改善推理。在本研究中，我們探討了一個互補的問題：是否可以通過加強隱含的視覺基礎來改善多模態推理，而不直接監督推理過程？受到注意力頭功能專門化的啟發，我們調查了是否可以通過僅引導對視覺證據基礎反應最強的頭來改善推理。我們提出了選擇性概率質量集中（sPMC），這是一個訓練框架，能夠識別對基礎反應的頭並有選擇性地正則化它們的文本到圖像的注意力。sPMC將對視覺標記的正規化注意力視為一種空間概率分佈，並鼓勵將概率質量分配給語義相關的區域，使用基於分割的空間先驗。自適應頭選擇將這種指導限制在對視覺有反應的頭上，同時讓其餘的頭保持不受限制，以保留其互補功能。在6個多模態基準套件中，sPMC實現了平均3%的零樣本改進，並在多個MLLMs中獲得高達11.3%的增益，同時僅正則化3%-15%的注意力頭。這些結果表明，對稀疏和隱含的視覺證據通路進行有針對性的指導可以直接改善多模態推理。
